history.prompt: Extreme close-up macro photograph of an intricate, makeshift relay bypass wired into a dark logic board. 100mm macro lens, razor-sharp focal plane on a single frayed copper wire slipping from a brass terminal block, while an adjacent indicator LED glows a misleading bright green. Visible surface texture, workshop dust, and metallic scratches on the circuit bed. Soft directional daylight mixed with warm amber workbench lighting. Shallow depth of field with the background falling away into deep shadow, hero object off-centre on the thirds, editorial elegance, sophisticated dark teal and copper palette.

style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration, technical drawing style, axonometric projection. An asymmetrical isometric layout with generous empty margin. A modular logic routing bay resting on a matte workbench surface, constructed from brushed metal chassis and frosted copper tubing. The assembly features a central validation gate module with one clear conduit and multiple blocked, stacked retry loops alongside it. Flat muted palette with a single amber accent colour, thin consistent line weight, one directional light casting a long shadow, unlabelled.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, watermarks, logos
rationale: The article focuses on systemic testing, routing, and validation architecture rather than a tangible physical product. A technical isometric cutaway perfectly visualizes the hidden structural failures and logic gates involved in agent tracing.
subject: technical isometric cutaway of a logic routing bay
composition: asymmetrical isometric layout with generous empty margin
alt_text: Isometric cutaway of a logic routing bay with a central validation gate and blocked retry loops.
caption: Repeat-trial testing exposes structural flaws in agent design that a single lucky run hides.
title: Agent Testing Pass-K Routing Cutaway
